ordered_diagnoses: Colorectal cancer liver metastasis with portal vein tumor thrombus

facts.raw_span: A 55-year-old man underwent right hemicolectomy for moderately differentiated adenocarcinoma of the ascending colon
staged as IIIB (T4N1M0)
He had no thrombophilic disorders
Preoperative carcinoembryonic antigen (CEA) and CA19-9 levels were normal
He completed six months of adjuvant chemotherapy
Thirteen months after surgery, follow-up CT revealed a 25 mm lesion in segment 8 of the liver
hepatitis B and C serologies were negative
Tumor markers including CEA, CA19-9, α-fetoprotein, and PIVKA-II were all within normal limits
CTA demonstrated a liver tumor with two components: a solid portion that enhanced in the early phase and washed out in the delayed phase, and a cystic component
CTAP showed absence of the right portal vein and a perfusion defect throughout the right lobe, suggestive of portal vein tumor thrombus
Endoscopic retrograde cholangiography showed no communication with the biliary tree
bile cytology was negative for malignancy

concepts.why: The patient has a history of colon cancer and now presents with a liver lesion, which is consistent with metastasis.
The liver tumor has a solid and cystic component, and the patient has a risk factor for HCC, although the tumor markers are within normal limits.
The CTAP shows absence of the right portal vein and a perfusion defect, which is suggestive of portal vein tumor thrombus.
The liver tumor has a solid and cystic component, which could be consistent with focal nodular hyperplasia, although it is less likely given the patient's history of colon cancer.
The liver tumor has a cystic component, which could be consistent with hemangioma, although it is less likely given the patient's history of colon cancer and the presence of a solid component.

The patient has a liver lesion and negative hepatitis serologies, which could be consistent with a pyogenic liver abscess, although it is less likely given the patient's history of colon cancer and the presence of a solid component.
The liver tumor has a cystic component, which could be consistent with a liver cyst, although it is less likely given the patient's history of colon cancer and the presence of a solid component.
The liver tumor has a solid and cystic component, and the patient has a risk factor for cholangiocarcinoma, although the bile cytology is negative for malignancy.

concepts.why: It explains the uncovered finding of a liver tumor with a solid portion that enhanced in the early phase and washed out in the delayed phase, and a cystic component, in a patient with a history of colorectal cancer.
It explains the uncovered finding of bile cytology being negative for malignancy, which could indicate a primary liver tumor other than hepatocellular carcinoma or metastasis.

rationales.F02: Advanced stage of colorectal cancer at diagnosis increases the likelihood of liver metastasis.
rationales.F06: New liver lesion on follow-up CT suggests possible metastasis or primary liver tumor.
rationales.F09: Liver tumor with solid and cystic components on CTA is suggestive of metastasis or primary liver tumor.
rationales.F10: Portal vein tumor thrombus on CTAP is highly suggestive of liver metastasis from colorectal cancer.
